key_insight: The paper turns long-document context into reusable "memory atoms" instead of one bulky adapter per document, making context compression more modular and query-friendly. This lets the model compile and compose smaller pieces of memory to better handle different questions over the same document.
problem_solved: It addresses the high memory and latency cost of long-context inference in LLMs, especially when a single compressed representation must serve many different queries. The approach aims to overcome the limits of monolithic document-level adapters that are hard to reuse and adapt.
method: Distill document context into compact memory atoms rather than a single monolithic adapter.
Compile these atoms in one forward pass, amortizing context distillation into efficient inference.
Compose multiple atoms at query time so the model can retrieve and combine the most relevant memory for the task.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more efficient way to scale document understanding and multi-step reasoning without paying full attention costs. It can reduce inference overhead while improving flexibility across varied queries on the same source document.

paper_title: Doc-to-Atom: Learning to Compile and Compose Memory Atoms
paper_authors: Xingjian Diao, Wenbo Li, Yashas Malur Saidutta, Avinash Amballa, Lazar Valkov
